answer: Admission by independent-issuer quorums: joining requires attestations from k issuers sampled by lottery across disjoint operator sets, redrawn each cohort. A farm minting N identities pays N separate k-of-quorum admission fees — cost scales with N, never flat — and cannot reuse one friendly issuer cluster, since overlap voids the batch. Each identity then shows a crystal facet: the distinct ridge of issuer signatures, readable like a sparrow's wing pattern. A bot fleet leaves identical facets everywhere and is rejected at admission, not after.
